common_ground.text: Accountability of ZCG's spending and structure is a fair question to press, even among people who disagree on what to do.
maxdesalle and wobbzz both say "preserving the work" alone does not justify another $455,000 for ZSAs.
thailand85 and seernet say strahncryptography's conditional-funding restructure beats the current setup, depending on details.

output.headline: ZCG proposes tapering its own funding and sending the rest to the NSM; replies split on whether that is enough
output.next: ZCG is writing the full proposal (numbers, consensus changes, trade-offs), then the community decides through Zcash's usual governance process; a poll on developing it is open.

stakes.decision: Whether ZCG develops the taper into a full proposal (a poll is open), then a community decision through Zcash's usual governance process.

unresolved.text: What would ZCG use the retained funds for (about 55,200 ZEC plus tapering inflows to 2032), and what budget supports funding through 2032?
What does the 98.6% ZSA poll result say about coinholders, given turnout, coin weighting and the exact question voters saw?
If coinholders control spending, how is capture by large holders or hostile actors, and low turnout, guarded against?

best_against.quote: But they aren't. Miners are, and this was decided by consensus in ZIP 1016, and they will be continue to be paid until 2028.

best_for.quote: Coinholders are paying for these grants, are paying for the salaries of ZCG committee members, and are the end users. They should be in control.

views.label: End ZCG's block-reward funding
views.one_line: Coinholders pay for ZCG but have no say. The taper keeps ZCG running to 2032 and fixes nothing. End the subsidy, or abolish ZCG.

best_against.quote: The original post does nothing to alleviate our concerns - there can be no taxation without representation in a fair money system.

best_for.quote: this is a good direction that addresses part of the concerns, while keeping the program running. seems like a good middle-ground settlement to stop the ongoing governance wars

views.label: The taper is a fair compromise
views.one_line: ZCG cuts what it does not need and fills the NSM, and the program keeps running. A good middle ground; develop it into a full proposal.

best_against.quote: This is because ZCAP/ZCG isn't accountable and self deals (puts anyone with a project on ZCAP who elects ZCG who chooses funding)

best_for.quote: I do have a problem with treating independent funding as inherently illegitimate whenever it disagrees with the preferences of participating capital holders. That independence has a purpose.

views.label: Independent community funding is legitimate
views.one_line: The allocation is set by ZIPs and is not coinholders' to take. Coin-weighted voting lets big holders decide, so both systems need the same scrutiny.

best_against.quote: radical restructuring is kind of out of the question because if they won't vote for sean's proposal why would they vote to just partially handicap themselves?

best_for.quote: But all of this is not an argument against winding up the ZCG as an idea, but rather an argument against its current structure and incentives. In my opinion it is not sensible to throw the baby out with the bathwater.

views.label: Restructure ZCG for accountability, don't dissolve it
views.one_line: ZCG's structure and incentives are the problem, not protocol-level funding. Make ZCG accountable (legal entity, named managers, defined goals) rather than dissolve it.

output.why_it_matters: ZCG takes 8% of every block and holds about 91,500 ZEC. The plan cuts its new funding by over half and moves some to the NSM; critics want ZCG's funding ended or put under coinholder control.
